history.summary: CSV town corrected from Purulia to Pakbirra (the village is in Puncha block, ~40-46 km from Purulia town). The Pakbirra Jain complex is a group of three stone temples built in tri-ratha nagara style, dated to about the 9th century, from the era when Purulia was an important Jain centre (6th-13th century). Nineteenth-century surveys by Beavan (1865) and J.D. Beglar (ASI, 1872-73) show the site was once a far larger Jain religious complex; Beglar documented nearly two dozen stone temples. The principal west-facing temple once housed a colossal 7.5-ft standing Jina (identified by the lotus emblem, attributed to Shitalnatha/Padmaprabha). Surviving sculptures include images of Rishabhanatha, Parshvanatha, Mahavira, Ambika and Padmavati, three votive ayagapatas, and a 'Sahstra pat' plate with 356 Tirthankara images; the Padmaprabha image is also worshipped by Hindus as Bhairavnath. An open-air sculpture museum holds the rescued statues. Coordinates are village-level (map geocoder matched Pakbirra village, Puncha, not an exact temple POI), so they are approximate to the village.

name: Pakbirra Jain Temples
town_description: Pakbirra is a small agricultural village in Puncha block of Purulia district, about 1.6 km east of Puncha town and 40-46 km from Purulia town, served mainly by private buses and shared autos. Apart from its Jain temples and open-air sculpture museum, the village has little infrastructure; visitors base themselves at Purulia or Raghunathpur.
